title: 2550M item 4: the TIN branch code prints three compartments, BIR's own runtime declares five

subject.description: The fourth (branch-code) group of the item-4 TIN comb chain on page 1. The chain prints 66.00-99.84 / 104.64-137.76 / 142.32-175.44 / 180.24-213.12, separated by three grey dashes 4.80 / 4.56 / 4.80pt wide. After the 2026-08-17 sitting the whole chain (not only this box) is reflowed to even 3-3-3-5 inside the original outer span; this printed box remains the PDF identity of the branch group.

match.strategy: the single element carrying data-field-kind="comb" whose emitted box equals printed_box_pt

subject.cell_id_hint: p1c13 at HEAD 98ca03c3 — NON-AUTHORITATIVE. Cell ids are quantised bounding boxes (lattice.geometry_subject_key) and renumber on any geometry change; 42 of 146 cited ids in the findings ledger are already dead (PLAN.md risk R2). If the hint and printed_box_pt disagree, printed_box_pt wins and the applier aborts. The applier binds to the batch by the comb element's exact bytes (957 bytes at HEAD 98ca03c3, occurring once), not by the id: a later batch that emits it differently makes the applier refuse rather than guess. That refusal has already happened once: the anchor first written against HEAD 77987f8 (954 bytes) matched ZERO times at 98ca03c3, and the record was re-anchored and re-reviewed against 98ca03c3 on 2026-08-17 rather than loosened to match both.

layout_policy.writing_box: outer TIN strip unchanged 66.0-213.12 pt; the four groups and three separators are reflowed inside it so every digit cell is the same width (3-3-3-5). The official printed boxes are knocked out with a white rectangle of that same outer span.
layout_policy.division: separators keep their printed widths (sum 14.16pt) and move with the groups; digit cells equal-split the remaining 132.96pt into 14: [9.5, 9.49, 9.5, 9.5, 9.5, 9.49, 9.5, 9.5, 9.49, 9.5, 9.5, 9.5, 9.49, 9.5]
layout_policy.slot_inset: none — even digit-cell width across the whole strip is the rule; re-applying per-group 0.36pt insets would squeeze the edges of each group and make the last five cells look different from the first nine
layout_policy.per_slot_input: TIN1/2/3: one editable maxlength-1 input per cell. Branch: five inputs, each value 0, readonly, so the printed branch is 00000 and cannot be typed over. The lock is authorised by the official artwork's own pre-printed 000 in this box and by nothing else.
layout_policy.note: Rounding is fixed here so the applier's output is byte-deterministic and re-computable by hand from the box width alone.
layout_policy.branch_lock: locked — the official artwork pre-prints 000 inside the branch box, so the corrected form reproduces that printed constant as five readonly zeros rather than offering a typing surface over BIR's own ink.
layout_policy.chrome: each digit group: one outer 0.72pt frame, white knockout inside. Interior ticks are short bottom hairs (~33% of slot height), matching the official charbox (2550M month v172), not a full-height wall on every digit. Separators: dedicated SVG fill + 0.72pt black frame, no input, not in tab order.

reason: BIR's February-2007 artwork for 2550M is CORRECT and OUT OF DATE. It prints three compartments for the TIN branch code and pre-prints '000' in them. BIR's own eBIRForms client, whose runtime this repository has harvested, declares that same field with max_length 5. No rule can derive 'BIR widened this field after 2007' from 2007 ink, which is precisely why this is a stage-2 correction and not a stage-1 producer bug (ARCHITECTURE.md, 'What belongs in which stage').

corpus_context.measured_on: 2026-08-08, all 53 bundles, from the pinned PDFs only
corpus_context.summary: 39 of 53 bundles print 3+3+3+5. Three print 3+3+3+3 — 2550M (Feb 2007), 2551M (2002) and 2553 (1999). One prints 3+3+3+4 — 1600WP (2010), branch box 218.52-276.00 with three ticks at 232.68 / 247.68 / 260.28. Ten are not measurable by this method and are listed rather than guessed.
corpus_context.correction_to_the_briefing: 2550M is NOT the only bundle printing 3+3+3+3, and the count of 3+3+3+5 bundles is 39 of 53, not 34. 2551M and 2553 print three branch compartments as well; 2553 declares max_length 5 in rules/forms/2553-v1999/fields.json (frm2553:txtBranchCode) and so carries the SAME defect, while 2551M has no harvested fields.json in this checkout and therefore has no in-repo authority at all. 1600WP prints four while declaring five. Those three forms are deliberately NOT corrected by this record: each needs its own record, its own evidence and its own review. Stating this here rather than quietly scoping to 2550M is the point of the record.
corpus_context.declaration_is_not_uniform_either: The HTA does not declare 5 everywhere: rules/forms/1601c-v2018/fields.json declares frm1601c:txtBranchCode max_length 3 while the 1601C artwork prints 5, and 1701MS / 1701Q / 2550Q declare 3 for their page-1 branch fields. So 'the HTA always says 5' is false and must not be used as a general rule. This record rests on 2550M's own declared value, not on a corpus-wide assumption.

filing_safety.harm: The return is filed against the wrong branch. A TIN's branch code identifies the establishment the VAT declaration belongs to; if it cannot be entered, the declaration lands on branch 000 — the head office — and the branch that actually made the sales files nothing.
filing_safety.who_is_affected: Every 2550M filer whose branch code is not three digits, i.e. any registered branch numbered above 999 (four or five digits). They have no way to enter it on today's form at all.
filing_safety.today: Three compartments, pre-printed 000, all three typeable: the filer can overtype 000 with a three-digit code and can enter nothing longer.
filing_safety.after: Five compartments over the same printed box; a four- or five-digit branch code becomes enterable, and the emitted value can carry the five characters BIR's own client accepts for frm2550m:txtBranchCode.

checks_that_must_report_it.expected_finding: the branch comb appears as an offender. The check compares the layout's slot count against the compartments it recovers from the source's own paint stream and, on disagreement, records failure kind `layout-printed-mismatch` with the reason 'layout has N slots but source prints M compartments' (audit.py:6660-6668); where the corrected HTML carries five slots against a layout that carries three, it records `invalid-emission` instead (audit.py:6812). five equal 6.58pt compartments laid across a box whose printed dividers stand at x 191.28 and 202.08 means at least one corrected input contains a printed divider, which is exactly what this assertion walks every input to find. It should gain offenders on 2550M and on no other form.
